newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand releases Cambodia's Sam Rainsy.
newsitem.headline: Thailand releases Cambodia's Sam Rainsy.

text.p: Thai immigration authorities on Wednesday released Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy after briefly detaining him as he tried to enter Cambodia.
"I will go back to Bangkok now," said Sam Rainsy soon after his release. On Tuesday Sam Rainsy slipped into the border town of Poipet to meet members of his opposition Khmer Nation Party.

Sam Rainsy came to the Thai-Cambodian border on Tuesday and called for resistance against forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who earlier this month violently unseated First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh from government.

He went to the Cambodian town of Poipet to meet 52 members of his party who, along with about 300 others from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, are holed up in Poipet, one of the last areas controlled by royalist forces in Cambodia.

A Thai army officer said Sam Rainsy's detention was initiated by the army, which then handed him over to immigration officials. The officer said Sam Rainsy had caused trouble for Thailand by using Thai soil to call for an uprising against the Cambodian government.
